claims.text: codex reads the model_catalog_json file during config loading, once at startup; the ConfigToml doc comment states 'applied on startup only'.
The read is a single fs::read_to_string of the whole file followed by one parse; no incremental read, retry, or content caching.
No file locking exists in the catalog load path; the models-manager's disk cache (models_cache.json, 300s TTL) concerns only the remote server catalog.
When set, the parsed catalog replaces the bundled one for the process; when absent, the compile-time embedded bundled catalog is used.
Nothing downstream re-reads the file: Config carries the parsed value, no path retained.
A nonexistent model_catalog_json path is a hard error: io::Error propagates through config loading; no exists-check, no fallback.
Invalid content is a hard error with dedicated messages; empty catalogs error likewise.
Empirically codex-cli 0.148.0-alpha.9 aborts before any model request on an incompatible catalog (openai/codex#38934).
Catalog schema is version-coupled and unversioned: the required supports_parallel_tool_calls field was removed on main; a catalog valid for one release can fail on another.
cc-switch#6661 reports the same class: Codex desktop 0.148.0 rejects a catalog whose entries lack supportsParallelToolCalls.
The debug models subcommand exercises the same startup catalog load path (the parse error in #38934 surfaces from it).
herdr's mod exec spawns directly (no shell, no env fixup): local commands inherit the app process's environment; a desktop-launched app carries a narrow PATH.
Remote-machine exec rides hc and therefore the target core's environment.
RC-mode launches resolve commands through bash -lic (login shell), so probe/launch environment parity requires the probe to mirror the launch form.
